correctness.rationale: The crucial fiber lemma is derived exactly: a degree-at-most-two vertex participates in at most one triangle; every base coloring has a nonempty connected admissible fiber; fibers of adjacent base colorings intersect because disjoint forced singleton fibers require changing both triangle neighbors at once. Induction therefore connects all valid colorings. A legal path to the global complement crosses a balanced red count, proving the parity-sharp bound for every graph order. Direct case classifications prove the six-isolated-state 3-degenerate obstruction, and the two cube plus two connector graph structure, state polynomial and diameter for books. The complete direct finite program separately checked 26,342 labelled 2-degenerate graphs of orders up to six, eight book instances and nine obstruction instances; those tests do not replace the infinite arguments.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A broad existence theorem for planar no-monochromatic-triangle colorings does not imply all feasible two-colorings are mutually reachable. A discrepancy bound for arbitrary triangulations cannot entail the parity-optimal bound for 2-degenerate graphs by restriction unless it already reaches parity, which the cited bound does not. Proper-coloring reconfiguration and triangulation-flip reconfiguration have different state spaces and adjacency, so do not subsume this claim. An older balancedness theorem already covers three-colorable triangulations as a balance-only case, so the novelty claim is restricted to all-states connectivity and the explicit reconfiguration classification.

The existence of a proper 3-coloring already implies the balanced no-monochromatic-triangle corollary by splitting one independent color class. Hence the balance statement is treated as a proven consequence, not independently original.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither prior balancedness nor proper three-colorability implies connectivity of *all* valid two-colorings under one-vertex flips. The fiber-intersection induction proves precisely that extra statement for 2-degenerate graphs, with a 3-degenerate disconnected counterexample. The balance corollary alone was known or easily derivable. The remaining open historical-risk is a generic constraint-reconfiguration theorem already implying the full fiber connectivity lemma.

originality.rationale: The main new claim is that every legal triangle-bichromatic two-coloring of a 2-degenerate graph lies in one single-vertex-flip component, with explicit sharp 3-degenerate obstruction and book reconfiguration census. Inspected prior triangle-coloring and discrepancy papers did not assert this complete solution-space structure. Balanced colorability alone is deliberately not claimed as new: it is known for three-colorable triangulations (Asayama–Matsumoto 2022) and follows easily from splitting a proper three-coloring into two classes. The original structural connectivity assertion and exact book-state graph were not found under actual primary and research-record searches. General NAE constraint-reconfiguration literature remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The principal structural theorem controls *the entire solution space* of a natural no-monochromatic-triangle coloring constraint: from any feasible coloring to any other there is a valid one-vertex-flip path, on every 2-degenerate graph. This is not supplied by previously known balancedness/existence, which we credit. The sharp 3-degenerate family collapses into six isolated states and arbitrary imbalance, showing where local fiber intersections fail; the precise book-family state graph, graph diameter and polynomial provide a nontrivial full reconfiguration census. The parity balance follows as a transparent corollary rather than an independently novel claim.
